  • Class
    Description
    AsyncRequestBodyTest
    Asynchronous handlers read the body of the request themselves, once, with AsyncRequestBody: decoded like a controller's @Body argument, with the same responses for failures, or streamed, with the limits of the server for buffered content applying only to what is decoded in memory.
    FilterInPlaceUriChangeTest
    A filter that changes the URI of the request in place, a filter method with a MutableHttpRequest parameter or a filter declared as a function, continues with the mutable request it was given: the route still sees the request of the connection, its remote and server addresses, its HTTP version and whether it is secure.
    FilterMutatedBodyTest
    A filter that continues with a mutated request whose body it set, even to null, is bound with that body, not with the bytes of the request: a filter can clear or redact the body.
    FilterRequestChangesTest
    Filters declared as functions change the request in place or continue with another request, like filter methods: a pre-matching server filter changes the route that is matched, a request filter changes the headers the route sees, and a request with another body is read by the body binders of controllers and handler routes.
    FilterResponseReplacementTest
    Response filters declared as functions replace the response, like @ResponseFilter methods returning a response: on a route, a group and a server filter, synchronously, on an executor and asynchronously, and the response filters after them and the client see the replacement.
    HandlerRouteAnnotateTest
    Annotations put on handler routes and groups with RouteSpec.annotate(AnnotationValue) and the other annotate methods: a FilterMatcher annotation binds its filter, directly or as a stereotype given in the annotation value, Version selects the route, later annotations override earlier ones, and the annotations layer over the ones of a bean method given with annotationMetadata(method).
    HandlerRouteAnnotationMetadataProviderTest
    The element a handler route has the annotations of, given with RouteSpec.annotationMetadata(AnnotationMetadataProvider), is the one an integration reads back from the matched route with MethodBasedRouteInfo.getAnnotationMetadataProvider(): a bean method the route implements, any other annotated element, or none, and the bean method of a controller route.
    HandlerRouteAnnotationsTest
    Framework features driven by the annotations of a route, on handler routes that get their annotations with RouteSpec.annotationMetadata(AnnotationMetadataProvider), from the annotations of a method only, or from the bean method the route implements: route versioning (Version), CORS (CrossOrigin) and its preflight, OPTIONS with Allow, filter binding with a FilterMatcher annotation, and a security-style annotation read by a server filter from the matched route.
    HandlerRouteAnyMethodMediaTypesTest
    A request of any method, standard or custom, that a route of HttpRouteScope.any(String) rejects for its media types is answered with 415 or 406, not with 405.
    HandlerRouteAnyMethodTest
    The routes of HttpRouteScope.any(String, io.micronaut.web.router.builder.RequestHandler): every method, standard or custom, behind a route of a specific method on the same path, an implicit HEAD route and a CORS preflight, and never a 405.
    HandlerRouteAttributesTest
    The attributes of handler routes, RouteSpec.attribute(String, Object) and RouteSpec.attribute(String, Object): the handler, the route filters and the server filters read them from the matched route.
    HandlerRouteBodyStagesTest
    The body stages of a functional route: an asynchronous handler of the decoded body or of the form, which is read before the handler runs, a synchronous handler of the body it reads itself, and the stages of a route of a custom method declared by its name.
    HandlerRouteConditionCombinationsTest
    The declarative conditions of handler routes, RouteCondition, and their combinations: the headers, query parameters, cookies and methods of a request, its host and client address as the server resolves them, and the time.
    HandlerRouteConditionsTest
    The conditions of handler routes, RouteSpec.where(RouteCondition) and RouteSpec.where(RouteCondition), built with RequestPredicates or not, and the RouteCondition of the bean method a handler route implements: a request that does not meet the conditions of a route is answered by another route, or as if the route did not exist.
    HandlerRouteConstraintsTest
    The constraints on the path variables of handler routes, constrain on a route or a group: a request whose path variables a route rejects is answered by another route, or with 404, never with a 405 of the rejected route.
    HandlerRouteFilterExecutorTest
    The executor of a filter of a route, of a group and of a server filter, chosen on the FilterSpec a filter method returns: executeOn runs the filter on the executor, like a filter method annotated @ExecuteOn, nonBlocking on the thread of the filter chain, and the last call wins.
    HandlerRouteGroupErrorsTest
    The error and status routes declared in a group of handler routes are local to the routes of the group, like the error routes of a controller that are not global: the innermost group first, then the groups around it, then the global error routes.
    HandlerRouteGroupFilterScopeTest
    The filters of a group apply to the routes of the group only, also to a route of another group or of the builder on a path under the same prefix; a server filter of the builder applies to every request its patterns match.
    HandlerRouteGroupFiltersUnmatchedTest
    The filters of a group are route filters: they run only when a route of the group matched the request.
    HandlerRouteGroupSettingsTest
    The media types and the executor of a group of handler routes, RouteSpec.consumes(MediaType...), RouteSpec.produces(MediaType...) and ExecutionSpec.executeOn(String): the routes of the group and of its nested groups inherit them, like the methods of a controller inherit its @Consumes, @Produces and @ExecuteOn, unless the route or a nested group sets its own.
    HandlerRouteGroupSettingsTest.Note
     
    HandlerRouteOrderTest
    The order of handler routes, RouteSpec.order(int) and RouteSpec.order(int): the route with the lowest order answers a request that equally good routes match, a controller route having the order 0; routes with the same order stay ambiguous.
    HandlerRoutePathlessTest
    Handler routes declared without a path, like a controller method mapped without a URI: at the prefix of their group, at the root, under the context path, with their implicit HEAD route and a 405 for another method.
    HandlerRoutePortPropertyTest
    The port of a handler route and of a group given as a property expression, RouteSpec.port(String) and RouteSpec.port(String): resolved like the port of a @Controller(port = "${...}"), including a default, and served on that port only.
    HandlerRoutePortTest
    The port of a handler route and of a group of handler routes, RouteSpec.port(int) and RouteSpec.port(int): the server opens the port, and the routes answer the requests on that port only, like the routes of a @Controller(port = ...).
    HandlerRouteRespondTest
    The routes of HttpRouteSpec.respond(HttpResponse): ordinary routes that answer with a response computed once, or created by a supplier or from the path variables, without a handler reading the request.
    HandlerRouteResponseTypeTest
    The declared type of the body of the responses of a handler route, HttpRouteSpec.responseType(Argument): the message body writer is selected for the declared type, with its type arguments, like for the return type of a controller method, not for the runtime class of the body.
    HandlerRouteResponseTypeTest.Foo
     
    HandlerRoutesAsyncErrorsTest
    Asynchronous error and status handler functions answer like the synchronous ones: the same errors of controller routes, synchronous handler routes and asynchronous handler routes (thrown by the handler, or completing its stage) reach them, and one that fails is answered with the default error response.
    HandlerRoutesConcurrencyTest
    Handler routes under concurrent requests: the route, group and server filters and the handlers are shared by every request, and no request may see the values of another.
    HandlerRoutesDocsParityTest
    The controllers of the documentation about request bodies, answered the same by handler routes: asynchronous handlers that read the body with AsyncRequestBody, and, where it applies, synchronous handlers that receive the decoded body.
    HandlerRoutesDocsParityTest.JsonPerson
    The person of the JSON examples.
    HandlerRoutesErrorsTest
    An exception thrown by a handler function is handled exactly like the same exception thrown by a controller method: by error handler functions, ExceptionHandler beans, the status of an HttpStatusException, or the default error response.
    HandlerRoutesPropagatedContextTest
    Handler routes run with the propagated context of the request like controller routes: an element an annotation filter with a MutablePropagatedContext parameter adds, e.g.
    HandlerRoutesTest
    Routes to handler functions, declared by HttpRoutes beans, run like controller routes: filters and error routes apply, bodies are decoded and encoded, GET routes answer HEAD, and a wrong method is answered with 405.
    HandlerRouteStreamingTest
    Streaming responses from handler routes: a Publisher body is written as server-sent events or as a JSON array, as it is for a controller that returns a Publisher.
    HttpRoutesServerFiltersTest
    Server filters declared by HttpRoutes beans with
    invalid reference 
    HttpRouteBuilder#filter
    : like @ServerFilter beans, they filter every request their patterns and methods match, ordered together with the filter beans, wherever they are declared.
    PatternVariableSpecificityTest
    A plain variable and a variable constrained by a regular expression at the same position are equally specific: a request both match is ambiguous and answered with 400; a request only the constrained route matches is routed to it.
    PropagatedContextParityTest
    The propagated context seen by a handler route is the propagated context seen by the controller route that does the same, with the same annotation filters: every scenario is answered once by a controller and once by handler routes, on the same path of two servers, and what the route, its continuations, the filters and the error and status routes observe must be the same.
    RootRoutingTest
     
    RouteGroupsTest
    Groups of handler routes, HttpRouteScope.group(Consumer) and HttpRouteScope.path(String, Consumer): the filters of a group apply to every route of the group, after the server filters and before the filters of the route, and only to the requests a route of the group matched.
